newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian troops reach rebel-held Albanian port.
newsitem.headline: Italian troops reach rebel-held Albanian port.

text.p: Italian marines on a multinational relief mission to Albania reached a key rebel stronghold on Thursday as diplomatic efforts moved forward to restore order in the anarchic nation.
International mediator Franz Vranitzky met Albanian President Sali Berisha for a second day of talks in the capital, Tirana, after cancelling a planned trip to the rebel-held southern port of Vlore.

A rebel leader in Vlore, Medin Xhelili, said he was disappointed Vranitzky had called off the visit and blamed Berisha, a target of hatred in the south for the chaos that has swept Albania during the last two months.

Former Austrian chancellor Vranitzky, now an envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, wanted to focus his two-day trip to Albania on preparing for elections, an OSCE spokeswoman said.
About 300 people have been killed and more than 700 injured in a spasm of armed violence that erupted after the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes and cost many Albanians their life savings.
The uprising began in the south and arsenals deserted by police and troops were looted.
The violence continues unabated.

Dozens of gunmen in the southern town of Lushnje fired wildly in a hospital on Wednesday evening as they grieved over the accidental shooting death of their friend. Although no one was hurt, the hospital was badly damaged during the rampage.
"There is no safety here," hospital director Agim Bezati said. "Everyone has guns here."
In the southern town of Gjirokaster, two men were found shot dead in a luxury car on Thursday morning. Police said they did not know the motives behind the killings.
A small force of 25 Italian marines arrived in the Vlore, 150 km (90 miles) south of Tirana, on Thursday morning.
They were first troops to reach the south since an eight-nation U.N.-backed force landed in Albania on Tuesday to protect emergency food and medical supplies.
The troops were warmly greeted by a group of about 50 Albanians, some of whom shouted "Down with Berisha" while the heavily-armed marines inspected the harbour.
"We are here to protect the aid convoys," said one Italian soldier named Salvatore as the sound of automatic gunfire in the distance echoed through the port. "This is my job. I am not afraid."

The Italian-led security force has already secured two key bridgeheads in Albania -- the western port of Durres and Tirana airport. Vlore is the third vital staging area. More troops from Greece are expected in Vlore on Friday.
A total of 6,000 foreign troops will reach Albania over the next three weeks. Italy said more than 1,700 troops have now arrived -- 700 Italian, 456 French, 350 Spanish, 120 Greeks and 153 Turkish.
Romania, Austria and Denmark are also contributing soldiers to the mission, codenamed Operation Dawn.

In Durres, where more than 1,000 French, Italian and Spanish troops landed on Tuesday, a boat carrying 213 more Italian troops arrived on Thursday. Sixty armoured vehicles and trucks rolled off the Italian naval vessel San Marco.
A spokesman for the Italian armed forces said it may take up to three weeks for all the troops to arrive.

"It will take us some time to adapt ourselves to the conditions in Albania," said spokesman Gianfranco Scalas. "We will need some time, perhaps three weeks, to adapt. We have to build camps, set up kitchens, canteens and toilet facilities."
